title: MPP Protocol Documentation
quote: The Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) is a protocol for machine-to-machine payments. It standardizes HTTP 402 'Payment Required' with an extensible framework that works with any payment network.

title: HTTP 402 Payment Required in MPP
quote: MPP services return HTTP 402 Payment Required to indicate that a resource requires payment for access. WWW-Authenticate: Payment id="abc123", realm="mpp.dev", method="tempo", intent="charge", request="eyJ...". Failed payment attempts return 402 with a fresh challenge and a Problem Details body.

title: MPP Challenges
quote: Challenges must be cryptographically bound to their parameters through the id field. The binding typically includes realm | method | intent | request | expires | digest | opaque, using HMAC-based IDs to prevent credential reuse with modified terms. request is Base64url-encoded JCS JSON with payment details.

title: MPP Credentials
quote: A Credential is a client's cryptographic response to a server-issued Challenge. Authorization: Payment [base64url-encoded credential]. Each credential is valid for exactly one request and servers must reject any replayed credentials. Components: challenge (echoed), source (address, DID, account ID), payload (method-specific payment proof). Tempo charge supports transaction (pull), hash (push), and proof (zero-amount) payloads.

title: MPP Payment Receipts and Verification
quote: A Receipt is the server's acknowledgment of successful payment, returned in the Payment-Receipt header. The Payment-Receipt header is optional; clients don't need it for correct operation. Fields: challengeId, method, reference, settlement, status, timestamp.

title: MPP HTTP Transport
quote: WWW-Authenticate: Payment carries the Challenge; Authorization: Payment carries the Credential; Payment-Receipt returns the Receipt. Challenges are serialized as auth-params in WWW-Authenticate using base64url-encoded JCS JSON for request and opaque.

title: MPP MCP and JSON-RPC Transport
quote: Challenges are delivered via JSON-RPC error code -32042 with message 'Payment Required' and challenge details in data.challenges. Credentials travel within the _meta field using key 'org.paymentauth/credential'. Receipts return in result._meta under 'org.paymentauth/receipt'.

title: MPP WebSocket Transport
quote: The client and server exchange payment messages in-band—no separate requests needed for voucher top-ups. When the channel balance depletes, the server sends payment-need-voucher and the client responds with fresh authorization. Messages use an mpp discriminator field.

title: MPP Charge Intent
quote: The charge intent facilitates an immediate one-time payment where the client pays a fixed amount and the server settles the transaction before receiving the response. Fields: amount, currency, description, expires, externalId, recipient. Tempo integrations add chainId and feePayer via methodDetails.

title: MPP Subscription Intent
quote: The subscription intent mediates recurring paid access. The client authorizes a fixed payment amount once, and the server reuses that authorization to collect at most one charge per billing period. Fields: amount, currency, periodCount, periodUnit (day, week, month), subscriptionExpires. Reuse is application-controlled, not keyed only on subscriptionId.

title: MPP Payment Methods
quote: Methods include Tempo (charge/session/subscription), EVM (charge, x402 exact flows), Stripe (charge via Shared Payment Tokens), Card, Lightning (charge/session, BOLT11), Solana (charge), Stellar (charge/session via SEP-41 and channels), Monad (charge, push and pull), RedotPay (charge), and Custom.

title: MPP Discovery
quote: Clients discover payment terms through a standard OpenAPI 3.1 document served at /openapi.json. Discovery is an advisory layer while runtime 402 Challenges remain authoritative. Extensions: x-payment-info (offers array with amount, currency, intent, method) and x-service-info.

title: MPP Identity
quote: When a server issues a Challenge with amount: 0, the client signs a proof message to demonstrate key ownership. No funds move on-chain. The server rejects transaction and hash payloads for zero-amount Challenges and requires proof. By default, a valid zero-dollar proof remains reusable until the Challenge expires. Identity extracted via credential.source compared against authorization records.

title: MPP Refunds
quote: In charge flows, refunds operate outside the protocol; the server sends the refund amount back to the client's public key. Sessions implement automatic refunds: unclaimed deposit returns to the client automatically. If the server becomes unresponsive, clients can call requestClose() and withdraw() after the grace period.

title: MPP Security
quote: If an attacker gets the key, they can mint Challenges that appear server-issued for your realm. Include a digest parameter for mutating requests. Use a shared atomic store when your server runs on more than one instance. Never log Authorization: Payment headers or Payment-Receipt headers. Zero-amount proof flows require explicit replay protection before production use.

title: MPP Tempo Payment Method
quote: Tempo uses TIP-20 stablecoins. Transactions settle in ~500ms with deterministic confirmation. Servers can sponsor transaction fees via a feePayer account, eliminating wallet friction. Intents: Charge (~500ms), Session (near-zero latency via payment channels), Subscription. 2D nonces enable concurrent transactions.

title: MPP Overview
quote: MPP was co-developed by Tempo and Stripe, with SDKs maintained by Tempo Labs and Wevm. MPP is an open specification proposed to the IETF. Three core intents: Charge, Session, Subscription. The very things that make these payment flows familiar and fast for human purchasers are structural headwinds for programmatic consumption.

title: MPP payments — Stripe Documentation
quote: MPP, the Machine Payments Protocol, is a protocol for internet payments. When a client requests a paid resource, your server returns an HTTP 402 response with payment details. With SPT payments, the server automatically creates the PaymentIntent when it receives a valid SPT credential from the client. Available to businesses with a US legal entity.

title: tempoxyz/mpp-specs — Machine Payments Protocol Specifications
quote: Specifications for the Machine Payments Protocol — powered by the 'Payment' HTTP authentication scheme. Modular: Core, Intents, Methods, Extensions. Specifications licensed CC0 1.0 Universal; tooling Apache-2.0 or MIT. IETF Draft submission as the core specification. Maintained by Tempo Labs and Stripe.

title: The Payment HTTP Authentication Scheme (draft-ryan-httpauth-payment-01)
quote: This document defines the 'Payment' HTTP authentication scheme, enabling HTTP resources to require a payment challenge to be fulfilled before access. Authors: Brendan Ryan, Jake Moxey, Tom Meagher (Tempo Labs), Jeff Weinstein, Steve Kaliski (Stripe). This I-D is not endorsed by the IETF and has no formal standing in the IETF standards process. Expires September 19, 2026.

title: MPP (Machine Payments Protocol) — Cloudflare Agents docs
quote: MPP standardizes the HTTP 402 Payment Required status code, giving agents, apps, and humans a single interface to pay for any service in the same HTTP request. Official SDKs in three languages (TypeScript, Python, Rust). MPP clients can consume existing x402 services without modification. Intents: charge and session (pay-as-you-go or per-token billing with sub-cent costs).

title: What Is MPP? The Machine Payments Protocol by Tempo Explained
quote: Agents deposit funds into an escrow contract (roughly 500ms setup time), then issue cumulative EIP-712 signed vouchers with each subsequent request. The server verifies vouchers via ecrecover with no RPC call or database lookup required, enabling sub-100ms latency. MPP sessions are payment-based (deposit escrow, stream signed vouchers, batch settlement) whereas x402's SIWx extension is authentication-based (prove wallet ownership, receive a JWT). Neither protocol has meaningful commercial volume yet. MPP reported roughly 31,100 transactions and $3,730 in volume as of late March 2026, explicitly flagged as unverified.

title: Tempo & Machine Payments Protocol — Parallel
quote: Parallel documents integrating Tempo and the Machine Payments Protocol for agent payments.

title: How Stripe MPP Lets AI Agents Pay for Your API — Zuplo
quote: The Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) charges for API requests, tool calls, and content with HTTP 402 payments co-developed by Tempo and Stripe.
